title: Return Values
description: Get results back from methods using return types. Learn when to use void vs. returning data.

slides.title: Giving Something Back 🎁
slides.content:
# Return Types

So far we used `void` – methods that do something without giving back a result. Methods can also **return** a value.

```csharp
int Add(int a, int b)
{
    return a + b;
}
```

The return type (`int`) replaces `void`. The method must use `return` to send a value back.

To capture the result:
```csharp
int sum = Add(3, 4); // sum = 7
```

options.text: Use the 'return' keyword to return a value of that type

quizData.explanation: All code paths must end with return and the correct type.

slides.title: Early Returns & Multiple Paths 🚪

quizData.question: Once a return statement is executed, the rest of the method is skipped.
quizData.explanation: Yes, return immediately exits the method.

slides.title: Common Return Types 📦
slides.content:
# Return Types You'll Use

- `int`, `float`, `string`, `bool`
- `Vector3` – for positions, directions
- `GameObject`, `Component` – for finding objects
- `bool` is often used for success/failure checks:

```csharp
bool IsPlayerAlive()
{
    return health > 0;
}
```

Use `if (IsPlayerAlive()) { ... }`
